item.title: AI biosecurity must include agriculture | Science
item.description: Advances in biological artificial intelligence (AI) have brought biosecurity to the center of public debate, and the US Congress is now considering the Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act (1). Yet this debate, like biosecurity more broadly, remains focused largely on human health and overlooks the importance of pathogens that affect crops and livestock. The United States and governments worldwide should prioritize crop and livestock protection by minimizing the likelihood of deliberate pathogen attacks and making the targets less vulnerable to harm.

item.title: India needs a tree conservation plan | Science
item.description: India holds 2603 known tree species, 650 of which are endemic, and 469 of which have already been assessed as threatened (1, 2). In October 2025, India’s Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change launched the National Red List Assessment, a 5-year, nearly US$10 million effort to evaluate roughly 11,000 species, including 7000 plants, against International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List criteria (3). However, identifying risk is not the same as acting on it. India should augment its substantial assessment investment with a conservation plan for the species found to be vulnerable.
